questions.element: two-ink pair treatment (--ember impossible end, --accent routine end) carried to every template
questions.evidence: none - concept round, no build (discipline rule 10)
questions.note: Relocation is judged on the surface as it reads, so this waits for pixels. The text-level signal: R9's iter-08 addendum reserves --accent for hover and focus and forbids it as a resting-state mark, and this concept makes --accent a resting ink on one end of every pair on every template.

Judged only from the packet text plus RULES.md R7-R13 and JUDGE.md; no pixel property was scored and nothing below a fold was inferred. The R-B challenge (leaders demoted to a trailing ledger) was judged as an argument per discipline rule 11 and routed to the keeper, not failed for being a challenge.

findings.problem: --accent becomes a resting-state ink on one end of every dated pair on every template, while R9's iter-08 addendum reserves accent weight for hover and focus and forbids it at rest.
findings.invariant: No element carries --accent at rest on any template unless it encodes a state, and the pair's two ends are distinguished by a channel other than accent.
findings.prescription: Distinguish the two ends by the kind word and position, keeping both ends at ink weight; or raise the rule change to the keeper under K14 with cause, which the packet does not currently do.

findings.problem: Collapsing /catalog to one line per row with a hidden-column chooser changes the surface R8's applied list names as rules-required, and the packet assigns it no class.
findings.invariant: The narrow /catalog form states its R8 class and justifies it against R8's test (does a value drift from its row) at the new row height.
findings.prescription: State that the one-line form keeps the row rule, since four columns on one line is exactly the drift case R8's test names.

findings.problem: Truncation with a title attribute is the packet's only stated remedy for a long model name at 390, and a title tooltip is unreachable by touch and invisible to the screenshot rig.
findings.invariant: Every row's record identity is fully readable at 390 without hover.
findings.prescription: Wrap the identity to two lines rather than truncate, and hold the chosen fields on one line.

findings.problem: Demoting leaders to a trailing ledger reads against R-B's named shape (a running board of the major players); the packet raises it as a keeper question but does not argue why proof outranks ranking for a first-time reader.
findings.invariant: The keeper rules on whether /frontier leads with proofs or with players before the finalist is built.
findings.prescription: Carry the argument into the packet rather than the question alone; the argument is the thing judged under K14.

diagnosis.strongest: HIER - the only packet with an explicitly ranked type scale, the lightest home door, an order on /wiki/<entry> that exceeds F-K12, and the round's best-declared catalog first-landing (R12's exact priority fields, one line, reader-chosen).
diagnosis.weakest: DENS - no R8 class is assigned anywhere, on a concept that materially rebuilds the one surface R8's applied list governs most tightly.
diagnosis.critical_issue: --accent at rest on every pair is a quiet violation of R9's iter-08 addendum: it is not raised as a K14 challenge, so it is a violation rather than an argument.
diagnosis.highest_value_improvement: Either drop --accent from the resting pair treatment or file it as a K14 rule challenge with cause; then state the /catalog R8 class for the new one-line form.

downstream.weakness: The concept's hierarchy is the best-specified in the round but its density decisions are the least specified.
downstream.cause: It reasons about the lead surface in detail and treats the index surfaces as reuse lines, so chrome questions were never asked per surface.
downstream.recommendation: If built, capture /catalog at 390 and /frontier at both widths first; the one-line row and the two-ink pair are where this concept either earns its density claim or relocates the noise.
